text:
oncall-bot: ALERT: Increased tail latency observed on inference-serving-prod. Auto-triage: KV cache eviction spike + batching backlog. paging @oncall (high). Logs: `kvcache.evictions=1.2M/min`, `batch_queue.time>95p=420ms`. Region: us-east-1.

Raj Patel: I'm on it. Confirming impact: which models/routes?

Elena Sato: Looks concentrated on /v1/generate (long-seq, multimodal warmup). Also seeing mixed short chat requests getting starved.

Sara Liu: Customer impact: two enterprise customers in prod reported degraded tail latency and intermittent 504s. Support has active tickets. @Maria Gomez can you surface customer names and SLAs?

Maria Gomez: Confirmed: AcmeHealth and SmartDocs had errors between 09:12-09:28 UTC. Both on Dedicated pools but routed through the shared orchestration layer. No data exfil. Notified CSMs, they want ETA.

Kevin Morgan: Quick hypothesis: a KV cache blowup caused memory pressure, which shrank continuous batching window and caused the batch scheduler fairness heuristics to prefer huge long requests -> head-of-line blocking for short requests. We saw similar before but not this magnitude.

Raj Patel: Can we triage live? Plan: 1) Add temporary per-route cap on max_inflight_requests for long-run models. 2) Disable KV prefix caching for the affected model to stop eviction storm. 3) Patch batch scheduler config to enforce short-request prioritization (lower wait time for small requests). 4) If not stable, scale pool and roll back recent runtime change. Anyone object?

Elena Sato: +1. I'll prepare a config snippet and a canary rollout to 10% traffic.

Sara Liu: If we can stop evictions quickly that's priority. How do we disable prefix caching without restart?

Kevin Morgan: We have a runtime flag `--kvcache-prefix-enabled=false` that can be toggled via the control-plane feature flip. Using `redwoodctl feature toggle kvcache-prefix --off --selector=model=long-gen-.*`. That should be non-disruptive.

Raj Patel: Doing that now.

deploy-bot: command received: `redwoodctl feature toggle kvcache-prefix --off --selector=model=long-gen-.*`

deploy-bot: feature toggle succeeded for 18 of 20 nodes, 2 nodes pending (retrying)

Raj Patel: Toggle reached 20/20. Eviction rate should drop in the next minute. Watching metrics.

(60s pass)

Elena Sato: Evictions down 94%, batch queue backlog down ~65%. Short-request p95 still elevated — scheduler still favoring long requests. I have a config patch to bias scheduler fairness.

Sara Liu: Paste the patch. We'll canary to service-group-a (10% traffic).

Elena Sato: Patch (batch_scheduler config):

```yaml
# canary patch: bias toward short requests
batch_scheduler:
  fairness_policy: weighted_age_plus_size
  weights:
    short_request: 3
    long_request: 1
  max_batch_wait_ms: 25
  per_model_queue: true
  short_request_threshold_tokens: 64
```

Kevin Morgan: Also clamp `max_batch_size` for long_request routes to 8. That prevents single huge requests from filling GPU slots.

Raj Patel: Applying canary now to service-group-a. Command: `redwoodctl apply -f canary-batch-sched.yaml --namespace=prod --selector=service-group=service-group-a`

deploy-bot: apply accepted, rollout started to 10% of pods in service-group-a

Maria Gomez: CS update sent: "We are actively mitigating; we expect improvements in <30m. No data loss. We'll follow up with postmortem."

(5m pass)

Elena Sato: Canary metrics look good: short-request p95 down from 420ms -> 88ms. Long-request p95 increased slightly (+30ms) but within SLO for those customers. No errors introduced. Recommend ramp to 50%.

Raj Patel: Ramp to 50% approved.

deploy-bot: rollout to 50% complete

Kevin Morgan: Also temporarily increased Dedicated pool size by +2 nodes to relieve hot memory pressure while we stabilize.

Sara Liu: Good call. Any sign of recurrence?

Elena Sato: Evictions stable at baseline. Batch queue length normalizing. Short/long fairness behaving as expected.

Raj Patel: Ok we can now flip the kvcache change back to default once reduced pressure? I prefer to keep it off until full postmortem so we can capture state.

Kevin Morgan: Agreed — keep prefix caching off for the long-gen family for now. We'll stage re-enable with a throttled rollout and observability gates.

Maria Gomez: Customer update: both customers acknowledge improvement, will monitor. No refund requests so far.

Sara Liu: Next: postmortem, RCA and action items. I want: root cause, timeline, why config allowed scheduler starvation, and automated detection to page earlier when eviction spike > X.

Raj Patel: Action items (initial):
- Short-term: keep kvcache prefix disabled for long-gen models until safe re-enable (owner: Kevin)
- Mid-term: add a safeguard in control-plane to auto-cap max_batch_size if batch_fill_time > threshold (owner: Elena)
- Mid-term: add an eviction alert that pages oncall at 5x baseline within 1m (owner: Sara)
- Long-term: enhance batch scheduler with explicit per-request latency SLO buckets and rebalancing (owner: infra/research)

Elena Sato: Will open PR for scheduler change and add unit + integration tests.

Kevin Morgan: I'll draft the postmortem and timeline and include the config diffs.

deploy-bot: rollout of batch_scheduler config at 100% complete

Elena Sato: System metrics look healthy across all pools now. p95 back to normal, evictions baseline, no new errors in last 10m.

Raj Patel: Marking this incident as mitigated. Moving to follow-up.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT MITIGATED: 1791234567 - KV cache eviction surge -> batching fairness regression. Severity: SEV2.

Sara Liu: Thanks team. I'll schedule a postmortem meeting and ping involved owners. Add logs/metrics to doc. :slightly_smiling_face:

Maria Gomez: I'll update customers with the postmortem link once drafted.

Kevin Morgan: Adding the final note: root cause looks like a combination of a recent runtime change to prefix caching heuristics + a traffic profile shift (short-chat spike) that together caused eviction hysteresis and allowed long requests to monopolize batches. We'll include regression tests for mixed workloads.

Raj Patel: Closing on-call. Good job everyone. :thumbsup:\"
